subject: Compilation Error for school example with RStan on Windows 7

messages.author: de0f441cbf692e7b
messages.subject: Compilation Error for school example with RStan on Windows 7
parts:
Hi,

I have previously used Stan on Linux and OS X without too much
trouble. However, I now am required to use Windows 7 for my postdoc
position. :-(

I was able to install RStan by following the directions
(https://code.google.com/p/stan/wiki/RStanGettingStarted). The c++ on
the fly example and RStan both were able to compile. However, when I
try to run the Stan school example, I get this error:


Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) :
Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! In file
included from C:/R/win-library/3.0/rstan/include/rstan/rstaninc.hpp:3:0,
from file121430ae55d2.cpp:6:
C:/R/win-library/3.0/rstan/include/rstan/stan_fit.hpp: In constructor
'rstan::stan_fit<Model, RNG>::stan_fit(SEXP, SEXP) [with Model =
model1214623358d_schools_code_namespace::model1214623358d_schools_code,
RNG = boost::random::additive_combine_engine<boost::random::linear_congruential_engine<unsigned
int, 40014u, 0u, 2147483563u>,
boost::random::linear_congruential_engine<unsigned int, 40692u, 0u,
2147483399u> >, SEXP = SEXPREC*]':
C:/R/win-library/3.0/Rcpp/include/Rcpp/module/Module_generated_Constructor.h:60:



I have included my version and session info along with the R output
with error message at the end of this email.

I searched through the Stan Google User group archives but was unable
to find anything for my problem. However, I did turn " verbose = TRUE"
in the Stan function and used set_cppo('debug') . If I missed a
previous post, please point me towards that post. I had trouble
identifying what my exact error is.

Regards,


Richard Erickson

Thank you clarifying that for me. Now it appears to work when I set

Yes. How much RAM does the Windows machine have? On Windows XP, you can right click on My Computer and go to Properties to find that out, but I don't know what the equivalent of that is on Windows 7. It is possible that with set_cppo("debug") that you exceeded the available RAM because debug mode adds the -g flag to the compilation to include the debug symbols in the resulting binary. Try opening Task Manager (again this may be called something else on Windows 7) and going to to Performance tab. Then try to compile the example under set_cppo("debug") and seeing if the memory expended hits the roof.

Ben

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Compilation Error for school example with RStan on Windows 7
parts:
mtune=core2 is in the R's system Makeconf files: for example, in file c:\program files\R\R-3.0.1\etc\x64\Makeconf.

The gcc in Rtools has a known memory issue.  One potential reason is that gcc in rtools is 32 bits program itself. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Compilation Error for school example with RStan on Windows 7
parts:
For the original poster, did you get through the installation of
Rcpp so that you could run the Rcpp example? It's a pre-req for
Stan.

More below.

- Bob

On 9/30/13 7:12 AM, R Erickson wrote:
> Dear Frï¿½nzi,

>
> Please reply to the group. It is good practice and will help others to
> who might have your same question. I have added the Stan user group
> back to the email conversation.
>
> To answer your question, I wasn't able to fix the fix the problem. If
> you read through the rest of the email conservation in the Google
> group, you'll see that we talk about compiler problems Jiqiang noted
> that:
>
> "The gcc in Rtools has a known memory issue. One potential reason is
> that gcc in rtools is 32 bits program itself."
>
> Ben gave me this line of advice:
> "...I'm not sure what the problem is, although if it is only a problem
> in debug mode then you should be okay to do research, provided that
> you don't write any buggy models.."
>
> I'm able to use Stan through R on Windows, however, I am not able to
> use debug mode. So, I avoid writing buggy modes... :-)

This is fixed in Stan 2.0 so that fast() mode reports
the same kind of errors as debug mode. In RStan 1.3, the
optimization level of the compiler was tied with the error
handling.

Debug mode is definitely problematic in Windows because compiling
with optimization level 0 (typically used for debug), blows out
memory.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: Compilation Error for school example with RStan on Windows 7
parts:
Dear Richard
thanks for your answer and apologize for my late reply and sorry for not being familiar with google groups! Hope this answer is posted to the right place.

I re-installed R in the "my documents" folder instead of the "program files" folder (there was a writing rights problem).
Then, I re-installed Rstan and the fast-mode seems to work well (the school example runs without warning and it produces results). The debug-mode does not work. But according to a message from Daniel Lee, this seems to be a general Windows problem. So, I do not care at the moment.

My C++ compiler give s warning that I would like to get rid of (even if this does not seem to be important). Would be very happy if somebody could help me (but is of minor importance since Rstan is working).

When testing the c-compiler as recommended on the RStan getting started page, I get the following error message (although R produces the “hello world” correctly).

cygwin warning:

  MS-DOS style path detected: C:/Users/Fraenzi/R-30~1.2/etc/x64/Makeconf

  Preferred POSIX equivalent is: /cygdrive/c/Users/Fraenzi/R-30~1.2/etc/x64/Makeconf

  CYGWIN environment variable option "nodosfilewarning" turns off this warning.

  Consult the user's guide for more details about POSIX paths:

    http://cygwin.com/cygwin-ug-net/using.html#using-pathnames


I probably found the solution on http://cygwin.com/cygwin-ug-net/setup-env.html:

“The PATH environment variable is used by Cygwin applications as a list of directories to search for executable files to run. This environment variable is converted from Windows format (e.g. C:\Windows\system32;C:\Windows) to UNIX format (e.g., /cygdrive/c/Windows/system32:/cygdrive/c/Windows) when a Cygwin process first starts. Set it so that it contains at least the x:\cygwin\bin directory where "x:\cygwin is the "root" of your cygwin installation if you wish to use cygwin tools outside of bash. This is usually done by the batch file you're starting your shell with.”

Unfortunately, as a non IT-specialist, I have no idea how to do this.

What is a "cygwin process"?

How can I set the PATH so that it contains “x:\cygwin\bin”? How does “x:\cygwin\bin” have to look on my specific computer? I did not find any folder with the name “cygwin”. Do I have to create such a folder?

Maybe you can direct me to a relevant reference?


Thanky you again for your help and best wishes
Fränzi

Am Montag, 30. September 2013 13:12:16 UTC+2 schrieb Richard Erickson:
Dear Fränzi,

Please reply to the group. It is good practice and will help others to
who might have your same question. I have added the Stan user group
back to the email conversation.

To answer your question, I wasn't able to fix the fix the problem. If
you read through the rest of the email conservation in the Google
group, you'll see that we talk about compiler problems Jiqiang noted
that:

"The gcc in Rtools has a known memory issue.  One potential reason is
that gcc in rtools is 32 bits program itself."

Ben gave me this line of advice:
"...I'm not sure what the problem is, although if it is only a problem
in debug mode then you should be okay to do research, provided that
you don't write any buggy models.."

I'm able to use Stan through R on Windows, however, I am not able to
use debug mode. So, I avoid writing buggy modes... :-)

Sorry that I cannot help you more. If you need more help, I would
suggest starting a new thread on the Google group and describing your
problem.

Good luck!

Richard

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Compilation Error for school example with RStan on Windows 7
parts:
The Windows (32 bit only?) tool chain for C++ is not powerful
enough to compile in debug mode (the debug instructions blow out
memory).

The Cygwin warning comes from outside Stan and I don't believe it's
under our control.

Could someone add some notes to the install instructions so our
users don't try to fix these issues that are both unfixable and
don't affect how Stan actually runs:

* Cygwin path warning out of our control, don't worry about it

* Windows (32 bit only?) can't compile stanc in debug mode

I don't have a Windows machine to test this on or I'd do it myself.

- Bob
